subject: Index hydration & rerank acceptance checklist
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
To: emma.sanders@librato.com
Cc: laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Index hydration & rerank acceptance checklist

Hi Emma —

Great to kick off this week. As we discussed on the call, the goal for Phase 1 is to validate a safe backfill strategy and an automated rerank acceptance signal before we flip traffic. To get the team aligned, can you send over a small export of the existing index metadata and a sample of ~1k vectors (with IDs)? That will help us run local similarity checks and a dry-run backfill.

Quick asks:
- Attach: current-index-stats.csv (schema + shard counts)
- Confirm: vector dimension and quantization (if any)
- Confirm: retention window for raw text (for PII gating)

Internal folks on this thread: Laura (CS lead on deployment), Sergio (inference infra), Naomi (rerank evals).

Proposed timeline:
- 4/20: dry-run hydrate to staging (no traffic)
- 4/21-4/22: run rerank evals & QA
- 4/23: production cutover window (tentative)

I'll attach a short checklist to the follow-up.

Thanks —
Connor O'Brien
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com
Attachment: current-index-stats.csv (CSV, 12 KB)

From: Emma Sanders <emma.sanders@librato.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>, laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com
Date: Fri, 16 Apr 2027 09:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Index hydration & rerank acceptance checklist

Thanks Connor — attaching what I can share from our side.

Notes:
- Attached: librato_index_manifest.json (index mapping + shard topology).
- Vectors: 512-d float32, no quantization currently; we're experimenting with 8-bit quantization on a separate branch but not in prod yet.
- Retention: raw text stored for 90 days, then redacted; fine for the staging dry-run.
- We have vector IDs that map to doc ids; we'll send a 1,000-vector sample by EOD.

Questions:
1) For a backfill to staging, do you want us to snapshot the current index or stream records? We can export an NDJSON with metadata+vectors if that helps.
2) For rerank evals, what format do you prefer for labeled sets? Naomi and your team mentioned CSV with query|positive_id|negatives.

cc: reid@searchly.ai (they're helping with the export tooling).

Best,
Emma
Head of Search Engineering | Librato AI
Attachment: librato_index_manifest.json (JSON, 28 KB)

From: Reid Carter <reid@searchly.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>, emma.sanders@librato.com
Date: Fri, 16 Apr 2027 12:01:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Index hydration & rerank acceptance checklist

Folks — quick operational note from the export team: streaming will be heavier on IOPS but can be rate-limited. For a 1M-doc backfill we recommend export + bulk load into your vectorstore (we support chunked bulk uploads). If you plan to use prefix/KV caching during the dry-run, expose the KV keys in the export so Redwood can validate cache hits.

Also: we can produce delta exports for daily sync. Pricing note: large exports may take 48-72 hours to prepare depending on shard load.

-Reid
Searchly Customer Success

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>, emma.sanders@librato.com, reid@searchly.ai
Cc: sergio_alvarez@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Index hydration & rerank acceptance checklist

Thanks Emma/Reid — this is helpful. A few implementation constraints from our side:
- Vector DB choice: for staging we'll load into a temporary FAISS cluster managed by Redwood Dedicated. For prod we plan to integrate with Librato's vector store via the connector (config TBD).
- Backfill approach: prefer export -> bulk load into FAISS (chunked by 50k docs) to avoid streaming throttles; Sergio can advise on chunk size & concurrency.
- Consistency: we'll run a post-load checksum (doc counts + sample vector similarity) and a small traffic shadow for 2 hours to check latency/throughput impact.

Sergio — can you draft the exact batch sizes, concurrency, and memory estimates for FAISS staging? Also add the KV cache verification step Connor requested.

Laura Bennett
Senior Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com, connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com, emma.sanders@librato.com
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Index hydration & rerank acceptance checklist

Following up with the infra plan. Highlights:
- Suggested chunk size: 50,000 vectors per batch, 4 concurrent workers.
- Memory: each worker needs ~24 GB RAM for 512-d float32 in FAISS with IVFPQ disabled. If Librato moves to 8-bit quant we can cut this by ~60%.
- Throughput estimate: ~120k vectors / hour per worker (rough), so full 1M backfill should be ~2-3 hours wall time with 4 workers plus overhead.
- KV cache validation: we'll include a sample of 5k prefix keys from the export and run a replay to ensure cache hit rate > 70% in staging.
- Safety: redact raw text fields in staging export; keep an id->hash mapping for traceability.

I'll attach a short checklist to the staging run and feed the metrics into the Redwood Console dashboards for per-route latency.

Attachment (inline): staging-load-checklist.txt

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com, laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com, emma.sanders@librato.com, sergio_alvarez@redwoodinference.com
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 16:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Index hydration & rerank acceptance checklist

All — prepping the rerank acceptance suite. Attached is a candidate eval matrix (rerank-eval-matrix.xlsx) and a 250-query sample prompt set. Key acceptance criteria I recommend:
- MAP@10 delta <= 1.5% vs baseline
- Precision@1 for golden queries >= 85%
- Latency: p95 token-generation + rerank < 350ms in staging shadow

Next steps:
1) Emma: confirm you'll share the 1k sample vectors and the NDJSON export by EOD so we can spin the evals tomorrow morning.
2) Connor/Laura: set the cutover window in HubSpot (HS-12345).
3) Reid: confirm export ETA & whether you prefer a daily delta sync or an incremental webhook approach after cutover.

Thanks —
Naomi Feldman
Applied ML / Evaluations | Redwood Inference
Attachment: rerank-eval-matrix.xlsx (XLSX, 95 KB)
